assumptions: Meeting notes primarily consist of rich text, headers, lists, and basic structural formatting.
The application is targeted at desktop and web platforms where users typically take meeting notes.
A single meeting note will typically have a small-to-medium number of concurrent editors (e.g., 2 to 10 users).
candidates: Block-based document structure to isolate user edits to specific paragraphs or sections.
Visual difference (diff) viewer to highlight merged or conflicting changes made by different team members.
Local version history/changelog interface to inspect, compare, and revert to previous states of the document.
Direct device-to-device synchronization over local area networks to share updates without public internet access.
confirmed: The product is a team meeting notes application.
Notes are stored locally on the device by default (local-first).
Notes can be edited without an active network connection.
When connection is restored, team members must see the merged content.
The merging process must not easily overwrite other users' modifications.

gaps.dependency: Requires deciding on the offline identity model (e.g., pre-linked accounts vs local profiles).
gaps.impact: Without verified identity, we cannot accurately attribute edits or enforce permissions, violating the 'not easily overwrite' requirement.
gaps.reason: We need a way to identify users and attribute their edits during offline sessions.

gaps.dependency: Requires deciding on the initial note sharing mechanism (online team space vs offline file transfer).
gaps.impact: Users cannot start collaborating on a note local-first unless there is a mechanism to establish the initial secure sync link between devices.
gaps.reason: The initial connection and sharing flow between team members' devices is unspecified.

options.impact: Low friction, keeps document flow intact, but leaves the user to clean up duplicate sections manually.
options.label: (Recommended) Automatically preserve both edits inline with visual markers, allowing users to resolve the text naturally during editing.

options.impact: Guarantees immediate cleanup, but interrupts the user's workflow during a live meeting.
options.label: Show a blocking conflict-resolution popup screen requiring the user to choose or merge changes before editing can continue.

options.impact: Zero workflow interruption, but users might not realize their offline changes were moved to history.
options.label: Automatically choose the latest edit based on local device timestamps, but save the overridden version in an easily accessible page history.

questions.question: When offline edits to the exact same text block conflict, how should the application present and resolve them upon reconnection?
questions.reason: This defines the core user experience for collaboration and directly shapes how the system prevents overwriting others' work.
questions.recommendation: (Recommended) Automatically preserve both edits inline with visual markers, allowing users to resolve the text naturally during editing.
questions.recommendation_reason: This prevents any data loss or immediate popup friction, keeping the meeting note editable while making the conflicting edits transparent.

options.impact: Ensures strong security and consistent user profiles, but introduces a dependency on an initial internet connection.
options.label: (Recommended) Require a one-time online login to link the device to a verified team account before allowing offline editing.

options.impact: Fully offline from the start, but lacks verification, allowing anyone to claim another user's identity.
options.label: Allow users to set a local display name and avatar directly on their device without any online login requirement.

questions.question: How should the application establish user identity to attribute edits, especially when working offline?
questions.reason: Establishing identity is necessary to label who wrote what and prevent unauthorized edits, but requiring online auth conflicts with the offline-first goal.
questions.recommendation: (Recommended) Require a one-time online login to link the device to a verified team account before allowing offline editing.
questions.recommendation_reason: This ensures secure edit attribution and access control, while still allowing full offline editing capability once set up.

options.impact: Highly convenient and automated, but requires a brief online phase before the meeting starts.
options.label: (Recommended) Create the meeting note on a shared team space when online, which automatically syncs it to all members' devices.

options.impact: Enables 100% offline note distribution, but increases manual file management effort for the users.
options.label: Allow exporting and importing note files (e.g., via local file transfer or messaging apps) completely offline.

questions.question: How should team members initially share and link a new meeting note before they go offline?
questions.reason: We need to define how devices discover each other or how the note metadata is distributed to enable subsequent offline syncing.
questions.recommendation: (Recommended) Create the meeting note on a shared team space when online, which automatically syncs it to all members' devices.
questions.recommendation_reason: This matches typical meeting workflows where agendas are set up beforehand, ensuring seamless transition to offline note-taking.

risks: Simultaneous edits to the exact same sentence or word by offline users may result in confusing auto-merges that degrade readability.
Data sync latency or loss if a user edits offline and closes the application or device before reconnecting and syncing changes.
Privacy risk if sensitive meeting notes are synced over insecure local network channels without end-to-end encryption.

tensions.description: Automatic seamless merging vs. manual review overhead.
tensions.reason: Fully automatic merges minimize user effort but risk creating grammatically or logically confused text. Requiring manual reviews preserves accuracy but increases friction for note-takers.

tensions.description: Local-first autonomy vs. real-time collaborative awareness.
tensions.reason: Working completely offline gives users freedom and resilience, but prevents them from knowing who is currently modifying the same sections, increasing the likelihood of conflict.

unknowns: How the system should identify users and verify edit permissions, especially while offline.
How notes are initially shared or linked between team members before they begin editing offline.
Whether non-text media attachments (such as audio recordings, images, or PDF slides) need to be stored and synchronized offline.
